text: In 1796, the scientist Edward Jenner injected material from a cowpox virus into an eight-year-old boy
ipa: /ɪn 1796 ðə sˈaɪəntɪst ˈɛdwɚd dʒˈɛnɚ ˌɪndʒˈɛktəd mətˈɪɹiəl fɹˈʌm ə cowpox vˈaɪɹəs ˈɪntu ˈæn eightyearold bˈɔɪ/
vi: Năm 1796, nhà khoa học Edward Jenner đã tiêm vật liệu từ virus đậu bò vào một cậu bé tám tuổi

text: with a hunch that this would provide the protection needed to save people from deadly outbreaks
ipa: /wˈɪð ə hˈʌntʃ ðˈæt ðˈɪs wˈʊd pɹəvˈaɪd ðə pɹətˈɛkʃən nˈidəd tˈu sˈeɪv pˈipəl fɹˈʌm dˈɛdli ˈaʊtbɹˌeɪks/
vi: với linh cảm rằng điều này sẽ cung cấp sự bảo vệ cần thiết để cứu mọi người khỏi các đợt bùng phát chết người

text: of the related smallpox virus.
ipa: /ˈʌv ðə ɹɪlˈeɪtɪd smˈɔlpˌɑks vˈaɪɹəs/

text: It was a success.
ipa: /ˈɪt wˈɑz ə səksˈɛs/

text: The eight-year-old was inoculated against the disease, and this became the first ever vaccine.
ipa: /ðə eightyearold wˈɑz ˌɪnˈɑkjəlˌeɪtɪd əɡˈɛnst ðə dɪzˈiz ənd ðˈɪs bɪkˈeɪm ðə fˈɝst ˈɛvɚ vˌæksˈin/

text: But why did it work?
ipa: /bˈʌt wˈaɪ dˈɪd ˈɪt wˈɝk/

text: To understand how vaccines function, we need to know
ipa: /tˈu ˌʌndɚstˈænd hˈaʊ vˌæksˈinz fˈʌŋkʃən wˈi nˈid tˈu nˈoʊ/

text: how the immune system defends us against contagious diseases in the first place.
ipa: /hˈaʊ ðə ˌɪmjˈun sˈɪstəm dɪfˈɛndz ˈʌs əɡˈɛnst kəntˈeɪdʒəs dɪzˈizəz ɪn ðə fˈɝst plˈeɪs/

text: When foreign microbes invade us, the immune system triggers a series of responses in an attempt
ipa: /wˈɛn fˈɔɹən mˈaɪkɹˌoʊbz ˌɪnvˈeɪd ˈʌs ðə ˌɪmjˈun sˈɪstəm tɹˈɪɡɚz ə sˈɪɹiz ˈʌv ɹɪspˈɑnsɪz ɪn ˈæn ətˈɛmpt/

text: to identify and remove them from our bodies.
ipa: /tˈu aɪdˈɛntəfˌaɪ ənd ɹimˈuv ðˈɛm fɹˈʌm ˈaʊɚ bˈɑdiz/

text: The signs that this immune response is working are the coughing, sneezing, inflammation
ipa: /ðə sˈaɪnz ðˈæt ðˈɪs ˌɪmjˈun ɹɪspˈɑns ˈɪz wˈɝkɪŋ ˈɑɹ ðə kˈɑfɪŋ snˈizɪŋ ˌɪnfləmˈeɪʃən/

text: and fever we experience, which work to trap, deter
ipa: /ənd fˈivɚ wˈi ɪkspˈɪɹiəns wˈɪtʃ wˈɝk tˈu tɹˈæp dɪtˈɝ/

text: and rid the body of threatening things, like bacteria.
ipa: /ənd ɹˈɪd ðə bˈɑdi ˈʌv θɹˈɛtənɪŋ θˈɪŋz lˈaɪk bæktˈɪɹiə/

text: These innate immune responses also trigger our second line of defense, called adaptive immunity.
ipa: /ðˈiz ˌɪnˈeɪt ˌɪmjˈun ɹɪspˈɑnsɪz ˈɔlsoʊ tɹˈɪɡɚ ˈaʊɚ sˈɛkənd lˈaɪn ˈʌv dɪfˈɛns kˈɔld ədˈæptɪv ˌɪmjˈunəti/

text: Special cells called B cells and T cells are recruited to fight microbes,
ipa: /spˈɛʃəl sˈɛlz kˈɔld bˈi sˈɛlz ənd tˈi sˈɛlz ˈɑɹ ɹɪkɹˈutɪd tˈu fˈaɪt mˈaɪkɹˌoʊbz/

text: and also record information about them, creating a memory
ipa: /ənd ˈɔlsoʊ ɹəkˈɔɹd ˌɪnfɚmˈeɪʃən əbˈaʊt ðˈɛm kɹiˈeɪtɪŋ ə mˈɛmɚi/

text: of what the invaders look like and how best to fight them.
ipa: /ˈʌv wˈʌt ðə ˌɪnvˈeɪdɚz lˈʊk lˈaɪk ənd hˈaʊ bˈɛst tˈu fˈaɪt ðˈɛm/

text: This know-how becomes handy if the same pathogen invades the body again.
ipa: /ðˈɪs knowhow bɪkˈʌmz hˈændi ˈɪf ðə sˈeɪm pˈæθədʒən ˌɪnvˈeɪdz ðə bˈɑdi əɡˈɛn/

text: But despite this smart response, there's still a risk involved.
ipa: /bˈʌt dɪspˈaɪt ðˈɪs smˈɑɹt ɹɪspˈɑns ðˈɛɹz stˈɪl ə ɹˈɪsk ˌɪnvˈɑlvd/

text: The body takes time to learn how to respond to pathogens
ipa: /ðə bˈɑdi tˈeɪks tˈaɪm tˈu lˈɝn hˈaʊ tˈu ɹɪspˈɑnd tˈu pˈæθədʒənz/

text: and to build up these defenses.
ipa: /ənd tˈu bˈɪld ˈʌp ðˈiz dɪfˈɛnsəz/

text: And even then, if a body is too weak
ipa: /ənd ˈivɪn ðˈɛn ˈɪf ə bˈɑdi ˈɪz tˈu wˈik/

text: or young to fight back when it's invaded, it might face very serious risk
ipa: /ˈɔɹ jˈʌŋ tˈu fˈaɪt bˈæk wˈɛn ˈɪts ˌɪnvˈeɪdəd ˈɪt mˈaɪt fˈeɪs vˈɛɹi sˈɪɹiəs ɹˈɪsk/

text: if the pathogen is particularly severe.
ipa: /ˈɪf ðə pˈæθədʒən ˈɪz pˌɑɹtˈɪkjəlɚli səvˈɪɹ/

text: But what if we could prepare the body's immune response, readying
ipa: /bˈʌt wˈʌt ˈɪf wˈi kˈʊd pɹipˈɛɹ ðə bˈɑdiz ˌɪmjˈun ɹɪspˈɑns ɹˈɛdiɪŋ/

text: it before someone even got ill?
ipa: /ˈɪt bɪfˈɔɹ sˈʌmwˌʌn ˈivɪn ɡˈɑt ˈɪl/

text: This is where vaccines come in. Using the same principles
ipa: /ðˈɪs ˈɪz wˈɛɹ vˌæksˈinz kˈʌm ɪn jˈuzɪŋ ðə sˈeɪm pɹˈɪnsəpəlz/

text: that the body uses to defend itself, scientists use vaccines to trigger
ipa: /ðˈæt ðə bˈɑdi jˈusəz tˈu dɪfˈɛnd ˌɪtsˈɛlf sˈaɪəntɪsts jˈus vˌæksˈinz tˈu tɹˈɪɡɚ/

text: the body's adaptive immune system without exposing humans to the full strength disease.
ipa: /ðə bˈɑdiz ədˈæptɪv ˌɪmjˈun sˈɪstəm wɪθˈaʊt ɪkspˈoʊzɪŋ hjˈumənz tˈu ðə fˈʊl stɹˈɛŋkθ dɪzˈiz/

text: This has resulted in many vaccines, which each work uniquely, separated into many different types.
ipa: /ðˈɪs hˈæz ɹɪzˈʌltɪd ɪn mˈɛni vˌæksˈinz wˈɪtʃ ˈitʃ wˈɝk junˈikli sˈɛpɚˌeɪtɪd ˈɪntu mˈɛni dˈɪfɚənt tˈaɪps/

text: First, we have live attenuated vaccines.
ipa: /fˈɝst wˈi hˈæv lˈaɪv ətˈɛnjuˌeɪtɪd vˌæksˈinz/

text: These are made of the pathogen itself but a much weaker and tamer version.
ipa: /ðˈiz ˈɑɹ mˈeɪd ˈʌv ðə pˈæθədʒən ˌɪtsˈɛlf bˈʌt ə mˈʌtʃ wˈikɚ ənd tˈeɪmɚ vˈɝʒən/

text: Next, we have inactive vaccines, in which the pathogens have been killed.
ipa: /nˈɛkst wˈi hˈæv ˌɪnˈæktɪv vˌæksˈinz ɪn wˈɪtʃ ðə pˈæθədʒənz hˈæv bˈɪn kˈɪld/

text: The weakening and inactivation in both types of vaccine ensures
ipa: /ðə wˈikənɪŋ ənd ˌɪnˌæktɪvˈeɪʃən ɪn bˈoʊθ tˈaɪps ˈʌv vˌæksˈin ɛnʃˈʊɹz/

text: that pathogens don't develop into the full blown disease.
ipa: /ðˈæt pˈæθədʒənz dˈoʊnt dɪvˈɛləp ˈɪntu ðə fˈʊl blˈoʊn dɪzˈiz/

text: But just like a disease, they trigger an immune response, teaching the body to recognize
ipa: /bˈʌt dʒˈʌst lˈaɪk ə dɪzˈiz ðˈeɪ tɹˈɪɡɚ ˈæn ˌɪmjˈun ɹɪspˈɑns tˈitʃɪŋ ðə bˈɑdi tˈu ɹˈɛkəɡnˌaɪz/

text: an attack by making a profile of pathogens in preparation.
ipa: /ˈæn ətˈæk bˈaɪ mˈeɪkɪŋ ə pɹˈoʊfˌaɪl ˈʌv pˈæθədʒənz ɪn pɹˌɛpɚˈeɪʃən/

text: The downside is that live attenuated vaccines can be difficult to make,
ipa: /ðə dˈaʊnsˌaɪd ˈɪz ðˈæt lˈaɪv ətˈɛnjuˌeɪtɪd vˌæksˈinz kˈæn bˈi dˈɪfəkəlt tˈu mˈeɪk/

text: and because they're live and quite powerful, people with weaker immune systems can't have them,
ipa: /ənd bɪkˈɔz ðˈɛɹ lˈaɪv ənd kwˈaɪt pˈaʊɚfəl pˈipəl wˈɪð wˈikɚ ˌɪmjˈun sˈɪstəmz kˈænt hˈæv ðˈɛm/

text: while inactive vaccines don't create long-lasting immunity.
ipa: /wˈaɪl ˌɪnˈæktɪv vˌæksˈinz dˈoʊnt kɹiˈeɪt longlasting ˌɪmjˈunəti/

text: Another type, the subunit vaccine, is only made from one part of the pathogen, called
ipa: /ənˈʌðɚ tˈaɪp ðə sˌʌbjˈunɪt vˌæksˈin ˈɪz ˈoʊnli mˈeɪd fɹˈʌm wˈʌn pˈɑɹt ˈʌv ðə pˈæθədʒən kˈɔld/

text: an antigen, the ingredient that actually triggers the immune response.
ipa: /ˈæn ˈæntədʒən ðə ˌɪnɡɹˈidiənt ðˈæt ˈæktʃˌuəli tɹˈɪɡɚz ðə ˌɪmjˈun ɹɪspˈɑns/

text: By even further isolating specific components of antigens, like proteins
ipa: /bˈaɪ ˈivɪn fˈɝðɚ ˈaɪsəlˌeɪtɪŋ spəsˈɪfɪk kəmpˈoʊnənts ˈʌv ˈæntɪdʒənz lˈaɪk pɹˈoʊtˌinz/

text: or polysaccharides, these vaccines can prompt specific responses.
ipa: /ˈɔɹ pˌɑlˌisˈækɚˌaɪdz ðˈiz vˌæksˈinz kˈæn pɹˈɑmpt spəsˈɪfɪk ɹɪspˈɑnsɪz/

text: Scientists are now building a whole new range of vaccines called DNA vaccines.
ipa: /sˈaɪəntɪsts ˈɑɹ nˈaʊ bˈɪldɪŋ ə hˈoʊl nˈu ɹˈeɪndʒ ˈʌv vˌæksˈinz kˈɔld dˈiˌɛnˈeɪ vˌæksˈinz/

text: For this variety, they isolate the very genes
ipa: /fˈɔɹ ðˈɪs vɚˈaɪəti ðˈeɪ ˈaɪsəlˌeɪt ðə vˈɛɹi dʒˈinz/

text: that make the specific antigens the body needs to trigger its immune response to specific pathogens.
ipa: /ðˈæt mˈeɪk ðə spəsˈɪfɪk ˈæntɪdʒənz ðə bˈɑdi nˈidz tˈu tɹˈɪɡɚ ˈɪts ˌɪmjˈun ɹɪspˈɑns tˈu spəsˈɪfɪk pˈæθədʒənz/

text: When injected into the human body, those genes instruct cells in the body
ipa: /wˈɛn ˌɪndʒˈɛktəd ˈɪntu ðə hjˈumən bˈɑdi ðˈoʊz dʒˈinz ˌɪnstɹˈʌkt sˈɛlz ɪn ðə bˈɑdi/

text: to make the antigens.
ipa: /tˈu mˈeɪk ðə ˈæntɪdʒənz/

text: This causes a stronger immune response, and prepares the body for any future threats,
ipa: /ðˈɪs kˈɑzəz ə stɹˈɔŋɚ ˌɪmjˈun ɹɪspˈɑns ənd pɹipˈɛɹz ðə bˈɑdi fˈɔɹ ˈɛni fjˈutʃɚ θɹˈɛts/

text: and because the vaccine only includes specific genetic material, it doesn't contain any other ingredients
ipa: /ənd bɪkˈɔz ðə vˌæksˈin ˈoʊnli ˌɪnklˈudz spəsˈɪfɪk dʒənˈɛtɪk mətˈɪɹiəl ˈɪt dˈʌzənt kəntˈeɪn ˈɛni ˈʌðɚ ˌɪnɡɹˈidiənts/

text: from the rest of the pathogen that could develop into the disease and harm the patient.
ipa: /fɹˈʌm ðə ɹˈɛst ˈʌv ðə pˈæθədʒən ðˈæt kˈʊd dɪvˈɛləp ˈɪntu ðə dɪzˈiz ənd hˈɑɹm ðə pˈeɪʃənt/

text: If these vaccines become a success, we might be able to build more effective treatments
ipa: /ˈɪf ðˈiz vˌæksˈinz bɪkˈʌm ə səksˈɛs wˈi mˈaɪt bˈi ˈeɪbəl tˈu bˈɪld mˈɔɹ ɪfˈɛktɪv tɹˈitmənts/

text: for invasive pathogens in years to come.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ ˌɪnvˈeɪsɪv pˈæθədʒənz ɪn jˈɪɹz tˈu kˈʌm/

text: Just like Edward Jenner's amazing discovery spurred on modern medicine all those decades ago, continuing
ipa: /dʒˈʌst lˈaɪk ˈɛdwɚd jenner's əmˈeɪzɪŋ dɪskˈʌvɚi spˈɝd ˈɑn mˈɑdɚn mˈɛdəsən ˈɔl ðˈoʊz dɛkˈeɪdz əɡˈoʊ kəntˈɪnjuɪŋ/

text: the development of vaccines might even allow us to treat diseases like HIV, malaria,
ipa: /ðə dɪvˈɛləpmənt ˈʌv vˌæksˈinz mˈaɪt ˈivɪn əlˈaʊ ˈʌs tˈu tɹˈit dɪzˈizəz lˈaɪk ˈeɪtʃˈaɪvˈi#abbrev məlˈɛɹiə/

text: or Ebola, one day.
ipa: /ˈɔɹ ibˈoʊlə wˈʌn dˈeɪ/
